title: CORSMiddleware & TrustedHostMiddleware: Header Validations and Host Header Attacks

progressiveExplaining.eli5: CORS middleware is a doorman who decides which other websites are allowed to talk to your API from a browser. `TrustedHostMiddleware` is an identity guard who makes sure the visitor dialed your real phone number, preventing attackers from tricking your server with fake hostnames.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `CORSMiddleware` configures Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) so frontend apps on different domains (e.g. `http://localhost:3000`) can access your API: `app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=['https://myfrontend.com'], allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*'])`. `TrustedHostMiddleware` guards against HTTP Host Header attacks by validating that the `Host` header matches an allowed list.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `CORSMiddleware` intercepts preflight HTTP `OPTIONS` requests before they reach route handlers, returning `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`, and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`. `TrustedHostMiddleware` executes at the outermost layer of the ASGI stack, checking `scope['headers']` for valid host patterns (`allowed_hosts=['example.com', '*.example.com']`) and returning `400 Bad Request` if poisoned, mitigating password-reset poisoning and cache poisoning vulnerabilities.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In `CORSMiddleware`, when an `OPTIONS` request arrives with an `Origin` header, the middleware validates `Origin` against `allow_origins` (or regex). If valid, it short-circuits and immediately returns a `200 OK` response with `Access-Control-*` headers without invoking downstream route handlers. In `TrustedHostMiddleware`, if the parsed host header does not match `allowed_hosts`, it immediately sends a 400 response and closes the ASGI connection.

codeComparison.title: Insecure Wildcard CORS vs Secure Origin & Trusted Host Setup
codeComparison.summary: `allow_origins=['*']` with credentials is fundamentally insecure; specific origins and `TrustedHostMiddleware` harden production APIs.

legacyOrBad.label: Insecure Wildcard CORS with Credentials
legacyOrBad.snippet: allow_origins=['*'], allow_credentials=True // ❌ Invalid and insecure configuration

fullFile.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

# ❌ INSECURE: Wildcard origins combined with credentials violates CORS specs
# and exposes API endpoints to cross-origin data theft from malicious websites.
app.add_middleware(
  CORSMiddleware,
  allow_origins=['*'], # ❌ Wildcard
  allow_credentials=True,
  allow_methods=['*'],
  allow_headers=['*']
)

from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.middleware.trustedhost import TrustedHostMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

# ✅ NEW: Guard against Host Header poisoning
app.add_middleware(
  TrustedHostMiddleware,
  allowed_hosts=['api.example.com', '*.example.com', 'localhost']
)

# ✅ NEW: Explicit origin whitelist for secure credentialed requests (cookies/tokens)
app.add_middleware(
  CORSMiddleware,
  allow_origins=['https://app.example.com', 'http://localhost:3000'],
  allow_credentials=True,
  allow_methods=['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE'],
  allow_headers=['Authorization', 'Content-Type']
)

interviewGotchas.question: Why will `allow_origins=['*']` fail in modern browsers when `allow_credentials=True` is enabled?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of the W3C CORS security specification.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: The W3C CORS specification strictly forbids combining `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` (wildcard) with `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` (cookies / Authorization headers). If a server returns this combination, **the client browser will reject the response and block JavaScript from reading it**. When `allow_credentials=True`, you must specify explicit, non-wildcard origin URLs (e.g. `['https://app.com']`).
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: FastAPI will raise a runtime warning or browser requests with cookies will fail if both `allow_origins=['*']` and `allow_credentials=True` are set.

interviewGotchas.question: What security vulnerability does `TrustedHostMiddleware` prevent?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks knowledge of web security and HTTP Host header attacks.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: It prevents **HTTP Host Header Attacks**. Attackers can send arbitrary `Host: evil.com` headers to a web server. If your application generates password reset links using `request.base_url` or uses host headers in caching proxies, the attacker can poison cache entries or trick the server into sending password reset emails containing phishing links pointing to `evil.com`. `TrustedHostMiddleware` rejects any request with an unrecognized `Host` header with a 400 Bad Request.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Always include `localhost` and your staging/production domains in `allowed_hosts`.
